title: Storing and reading data
summary: One PostgreSQL database with TimescaleDB holds two schemas. Laravel owns public; the Go runtime owns device_runtime and is the only writer of readings. The top row writes, the middle row is the tables, and the bottom row is how data is read back and removed.

boxes.label: Storage consumer
boxes.detail: Takes one mapped telemetry message at a time from JetStream and stores it in a single transaction: readings, latest values, the committed outbox row and the hour's usage count in usage_data_points.

boxes.label: Outbox relays
boxes.detail: Two relays read unpublished rows oldest first, publish each to JetStream and mark it published once the broker accepts it. telemetry_outbox feeds the committed telemetry stream; outbox feeds the stream whose consumer posts lifecycle events to Laravel.

boxes.label: Automation evaluator
boxes.detail: Evaluates committed telemetry. Execution state, the stream checkpoint and the events it raises commit together, so a redelivered input changes nothing.

boxes.label: Control consumer
boxes.detail: Applies what Laravel asks for. Each applied device is saved with its definition and applied generation, and the confirmation event is written to the outbox in the same transaction.

boxes.label: Outboxes
boxes.detail: outbox holds lifecycle events for Laravel. telemetry_outbox holds every stored message in sequence order and never enters the Laravel inbox. Its unique telemetry_uuid is also the ledger that stops a redelivered message from being stored twice.

boxes.label: Automation state
boxes.detail: Rule and DAG executions, the single checkpoint row for the committed stream, consumed-input markers, transitions, intents, the DAG clock and the evaluation timeline. Only the evaluation timeline follows an organization's retention.

boxes.label: Runtime bookkeeping
boxes.detail: devices is the applied definition and generation of each device: storing a reading checks it first. commands tracks requests that are dispatching or sent. connectivity has one row per monitored subject for offline detection, never one per packet. usage_data_points counts stored readings per organization and UTC hour.

boxes.label: public schema
boxes.detail: Created by Laravel migrations: organizations, devices and their configurations, device_outbox and device_inbox, retention settings, billing usage. No reading is stored here.

boxes.label: Laravel API
boxes.detail: Reads and writes its own schema with Eloquent. For readings it calls the runtime's internal HTTP endpoints with a shared bearer token and never queries the reading tables for people.

steps.text: The storage consumer is the only writer of readings. One transaction per message writes observations or diagnostics and the latest values.
The same transaction adds the message to telemetry_outbox. Its unique ID is the ledger: a redelivered message stops there.
The relays publish unpublished rows in order and mark them published. Everything downstream of storage starts from these rows.
The automation evaluator keeps its execution state and its stream checkpoint in the same schema and commits them together.
Transitions and intents leave as rows in outbox, written in that same transaction.
The control consumer records which configuration and generation each device runs. A reading for any other generation is not stored.
Laravel keeps what people configure in its own schema, in the same database: devices, configurations, retention settings.
To show readings, Laravel authorizes the request and then asks the runtime over internal HTTP. It adds the organization and its retention to every query.
The runtime answers latest values from latest and history from observations.
A resumed application telemetry stream is caught up from telemetry_outbox by sequence.
The boundary leaks in two places: Laravel's operations metrics read device_runtime tables, and the restore quarantine command updates commands.
Once a day the maintenance loop deletes each organization's readings older than its retention, and prunes outboxes, ledgers and usage buckets.
